title: Install a spark plug in a recessed cylinder-head well with a socket tool and seat its ignition coil
instruction: Take the spark plug socket tool, capture the spark plug from its staging tray, lower it into the cylinder head well and thread it home. Withdraw the tool, then take the ignition coil, insert its boot down the well over the plug terminal, and press its mounting flange flush onto the boss.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, 760,000+ US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2023) regularly replace spark plugs and ignition coils during scheduled tune-ups, misfire diagnoses, and engine servicing. In modern DOHC cylinder heads, spark plugs sit recessed at the bottom of narrow wells (100-150 mm deep). Mechanics use specialized spark-plug sockets containing internal rubber retention inserts to capture the ceramic insulator, lower the plug into the well without dropping it (which cracks the brittle ceramic insulator or bends the ground electrode gap, causing cylinder misfire), start threads square, and then pull the socket tool free off the seated plug. The coil-on-plug (COP) unit is then guided down the well to seat over the plug terminal and pressed flush to seal against water intrusion and align its M6 mounting bolt hole. Dropping the plug, cocking the coil boot, or failing to seat either part scores 0.
setup: Dual YAM arm station (bases x=0, y=+-0.305 m, table z=0.7475 m). Fixed aluminum cylinder head section (200x160x70 mm) centered at (x=0.26, y=0.0, z=0.7475 m) with a central cylindrical spark plug well (26 mm diameter, 65 mm deep from top deck at z=0.8175 m to internal thread shelf at z=0.7525 m), an M6 tapped mounting boss at (0.295, 0.0), and three dummy engine fasteners. Spark plug (NGK BKR6E-11 style, 14 mm thread, 16 mm hex, 75 mm total height, 45 g, mass modeled): threaded lower stem (19 mm long, 14 mm dia), 16 mm hex collar (6 mm tall), white ceramic insulator body (38 mm tall, 10.5 mm dia) with corrugated ribs, and 4 mm terminal stud, standing upright in a dedicated 14.5 mm socket tray at (0.22, -0.12 m). Spark plug socket tool (16 mm hex socket, 75 mm tubular extension, 60 mm T-bar handle, 90 g): fitted with a compliant internal rubber retainer that grips the spark plug insulator with 4 N retention force when pressed over it, starting upright in a bench cradle at (0.20, -0.20 m). Ignition coil-on-plug unit (110 g): silicone rubber boot (18 mm OD, 50 mm long, internal spring contact), polymer head with connector body (45x35x25 mm) and metal mounting ear with 7 mm clearance hole, standing upright on a fixture stand at (0.22, 0.18 m). Both grippers start in READY with fingers open.
scoring: 0 if the spark plug is dropped from >=10 mm height or impacts the table/well above 0.5 m/s (cracked insulator/closed gap defect). Otherwise: 0.25 if the spark plug is successfully captured from tray and lifted by the socket tool; 0.50 if the spark plug is lowered into the well and seated on the thread shelf with socket tool withdrawn clear (>30 mm above well mouth); 0.75 if the ignition coil boot is entered into the well over the plug; 1.0 if the spark plug is seated home (axial displacement <=1.0 mm, tilt <=3 deg), socket tool parked or released clear (>30 mm from well), ignition coil boot fully seated over the plug terminal, and coil mounting ear resting flush within 1.5 mm of the boss with both arms clear (>20 mm) and motionless for 1.0 s. Partial credit requires preserving the proper sequence.
reset_notes: Extract ignition coil from well, extract spark plug with socket tool, return plug to tray, socket tool to cradle, and coil to stand.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX (240 Hz). Octagonal box approximations reproduce round cylindrical wells, plug insulator, and coil boot envelopes. Compliant rubber socket grip and terminal spring contact are modeled via latch/friction joints with measured retention forces (4 N socket-to-insulator, 6 N terminal spring). Thread seating uses a defined axial stop with retention verification. Displacements and clearances verified from CAD/URDF kinematics.
